speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for National Development how does HDB determine what qualifies as over-crowding in HDB flats and whether Minimum Space Standards, or similar objective criteria, can be published to improve transparency.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: However, HDB imposes an occupancy cap on flats which are rented out to unrelated persons.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is to minimise the disamenities caused by overcrowding and to maintain a conducive living environment in our public housing estates.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: HDB reviews the occupancy cap from time to time to ensure that it remains relevant.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Appropriate action will be taken against the flat owners if the number of tenants exceeds the occupancy cap.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will the Minister consider using this maximum number of occupants allowed in a flat that is being rented out as the same criteria to be applied when the single unwed parent or a divorcee is considered whether they can live with their parents or family members as an alternative accommodation?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am suggesting this as this would make sense if the family wanted to rent out the flat and they are not allowed to because they have met the maximum number of occupant limits and would be considered overcrowded.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I also asked in the Parliamentary Question about the minimum space standard.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister clarify why we are not going to publish this minimum space standard?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This is what is actually being done in the European Union and Canada already.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Not all countries have a minimum space standard and, even those that do, use these standards as guidelines.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are not necessarily legislated in some of the countries that Mr Louis Ng mentioned.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In Singapore's context, all of us know that space is limited and we have to optimise space to the best of our abilities.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have residents from Nee Soon Group Representation Constituency requesting for it because we have some old jumbo flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, I vaguely recall, and I stand corrected if my memory is wrong, that we had an earlier debate on this under the Planning Act, and it was Er Dr Lee herself.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, Er Dr Lee has now asked for more flexibility for the jumbo flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will have to look at whether or not this is feasible.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we have aligned the standards between HDB and URA; and it is a standard of six for the larger flat types in the HDB case presently.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: We talk about over-crowding and I cannot see a reason why whether a person is related or not would determine whether the place is over-crowded.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: If there are nine people staying in there who are related, it would still be over-crowded, even if the nine people were unrelated.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: So, can the Minister clarify why there is this point about whether they are related or not, in terms of deciding whether it is over-crowded?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It may be a family with five children, three children, four children, what flat type you wish to choose is entirely up to you.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are generous grants given, and then you decide what flat you choose.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is a policy that has served us well and will remain.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why there is this occupancy cap and it is applied to unrelated persons.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Yes, Minister, I support the change to cap the number of people in rented HDB flat because HDB flats are mainly for people to stay in.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: But what I am requesting for review are those jumbo flats because it consists of one 4-room flat and one 3-room flat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Based on current ruling, 4-room you can lease out to six, 3-room you can lease out to six, so it is 12 in total, actually.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: But the Ministry of National Development has put it together and caps it at six only.
